Standards for Teaching Room and Common Area
General
Teaching Rooms set up requirements are communicated to the Portering Team via the Operations Diary and also via individual organisers advising the Team Leader
Procedure
Porters will undertake teaching room audits at the start of the 7am shift. (See APPENDIX 14 Department Handbooks).
These checks are to ensure rooms are set to the required default arrangement and to a high standard. Any issue(s) identified while undertaking these audits should be reported to the Duty Manager As Soon As Possible and completed forms are to be submitted to the Team Leader upon their arrival at 8am.
Before setting up rooms it is imperative that the Portering team liaise/communicate with the Team Leader to obtain the most up to date room plans
Health and Safety
The following points must be adhered too when carrying out room set-ups. This is to ensure that you maintain a safe working environment:

source: Sammy Ofer Centre Check List (Section 3) copy - Copy.docx
text:
Manual Handling requirements
Health and Safety in the work place
Use of appropriate equipment when moving or storing furniture.
The condition and availability of the furniture that is being used
Protecting the fabric of the building (walls, doors etc.) when moving furniture
When handling furniture and equipment, due care must be taken to ensure that items are moved in such a way as to protect the items, so that they do not get damaged in transit
Furniture stock should be stored in an orderly way so that items are easily accessible.
NB: Outdated teaching materials are to be removed from the Lecture theatre and teaching rooms upon servicing. All such teaching materials are to be investigated with Team leader before discarded.
The Lounge
Sofas and Armchairs are to be arranged horizontally to the edge of the rug with coffee tables positioned centrally.
Consider Traffic Flow. One of the most important things to consider when arranging furniture in any room is traffic flow. People should not be tripping over furniture, or each other, to pass through the room. Make sure there are a couple feet (give or take a few inches) between the coffee table and sofa, and between chairs. Create a clear path so people can walk from one end of the room to the other without difficulty.

Receptions, Lobbies and Communal Spaces
Sofas and Armchairs are to be arranged horizontal to the edge of the rug with coffee tables positioned centrally.
Consider Traffic Flow. One of the most important things to consider when arranging furniture in any room is traffic flow. People should not be tripping over furniture, or each other to pass through the room. Make sure there are a couple of feet (give or take a few inches) between the coffee table and sofa and between chairs. Create a clear path so people can walk from one end of the room to the other without difficulty.
Lecture Theatres, Boardrooms and Seminar Rooms.
Chairs are to be adjusted and levelled to the highest point with armrests positioned over the desk top. See example below. Where chairs arm are not able to position above the desk top, it then becomes imperative that chairs are kept a small distance from the edge of the worktop to prevent wear and tear to both the chairs as table.
